pcs.pc_description: Review the customer complaint or service request and confirm details with the customer.
Prepare for the visit by collecting tools, manuals, and relevant information.
Greet the customer professionally, maintain personal hygiene, and communicate politely.
Check product details like warranty, service history, and gather information on the issue.
Explain the problem, suggest solutions with time and cost estimates, and seek customer approval.
Complete post-interaction tasks such as documentation, follow-up, and providing preventive guidance.
Follow standard electrical safety practices (as per IS 5216), including power isolation, use of insulated tools, voltage testing, and avoiding work in damp environments.
Adhere to occupational health and safety protocols (ISO 45001) by using PPE, ensuring ergonomic posture, and handling tools safely to prevent injuries.
Implement fire safety measures (IS 1646/NBC), such as identifying overheating risks, avoiding overloading, and keeping appropriate fire extinguishers accessible.
Maintain a clean and hazard-free work area (IS 14489) and dispose of damaged parts as per CPCB guidelines under E-Waste Management Rules, 2022.

modules.module_title: Apply Basic Electrical Concepts and Practices

pcs.pc_description: Identify and explain fundamental electrical terms and principles such as voltage, current, resistance, power, and apply Ohm’s Law in basic calculations.
Recognize different types of electrical circuits (series, parallel, combination), conductors and insulators, and describe their roles in domestic wiring systems.
Identify common wire types, domestic wiring components, and protection devices such as fuses, MCBs, ELCBs, and circuit breakers and explain their uses.
Calculate basic electrical energy consumption using appropriate formulas, and interpret energy meter readings.
Use electrical testing instruments like multimeter, clamp meter, megger, and capacitor meter to measure basic electrical parameters and check circuit continuity/safety.

modules.module_title: Familiarize with Fan and Cooler Types, Parts, and Working Principles

pcs.pc_description: Identify different types of fans (wall, table, pedestal, exhaust,BLDC) and coolers (desert, window, personal, tower), along with their common parts and working principles.
Explain the function of key components such as motors, capacitors, pumps, blades, switches, fuses, and gaskets.
Follow manufacturer instructions and safety precautions for disassembling and assembling units.

modules.module_title: Diagnose Faults in Fans and Coolers

pcs.pc_description: Interact with the customer to understand usage patterns and observe for symptoms like noise, overheating, water leakage, or failure to operate.
Turn off power supply, unplug the appliance, and perform basic inspections and electrical tests (earth test, continuity, fuse check, component testing).
Detect mechanical or electrical faults in key modules — motor, capacitor, pump, wiring, switch, or power cord — using appropriate tools.
Isolate and inspect each module separately if the issue is not resolved through basic tests.
Escalate to service centre/workshop if fault requires advanced diagnosis beyond site-level capability.
Repair or replace faulty components (motor, capacitor, pump, switch, fuse, blade) on-site as per standard procedures.
Schedule a follow-up visit if component replacement is not possible at the customer's location.
Reassemble the unit and verify full functionality post repair.
Demonstrate the functionality of the repaired unit to the customer and explain preventive care and cleaning procedures.
Fill customer acknowledgment form, update service records, and close the complaint as per documentation protocols.
Collect payment and promote related services/products such as AMC or new appliances as per company policy.
Follow warranty terms, and advise customer on service coverage or exclusions based on product warranty policy.

pcs.pc_description: Identify different types of lighting systems such as solar LED lights, emergency lights, tube lights, and panel lights.
Explain working principles: conversion of solar energy to electrical energy through PV panels, battery storage, and LED illumination.
Describe common components: solar panel, LED module, battery, charge controller, driver circuit, sensors, switches, and connectors.
Use appropriate tools: multimeter, clamp meter, screwdriver set, soldering iron, and cleaning brush.
Follow safety precautions: disconnect power, use insulated tools and PPE, prevent short circuits, and avoid overcharging batteries
Interact with customers to identify complaints such as light not turning on, dim illumination, battery not charging, or flickering.
Inspect the unit visually for loose connections, corrosion, damaged wires, broken LEDs, or dust accumulation on solar panels.
Conduct basic tests: measure panel voltage, battery output, LED continuity, and driver circuit functionality.
Identify and replace faulty components like LED modules, drivers, fuses, switches, wires, solar panels, or batteries using recommended tools.
Reassemble parts ensuring secure electrical connections, proper insulation, and correct polarity of solar and battery terminals.
Test the system under sunlight or simulated power source for charging efficiency, illumination level, and auto on/off functionality.
Demonstrate repaired light to the customer, explain maintenance practices like cleaning panels and avoiding deep battery discharge, complete documentation, and ensure work area cleanliness.

pcs.pc_description: Identify models and key components of electric kettles, steam irons, and garment steamers.
Explain working principles: resistive heating (kettle) and steam generation via heating element and water tank (iron/steamer).
Describe common parts: heating coil, thermostat, indicator lamp, power cord, thermal fuse, steam vent, spray nozzle, base plate, gasket, and switches
Use appropriate tools such as multimeter, clamp meter, screwdrivers, pliers, and cleaning cloth.
Follow safety precautions: disconnect power, use PPE, prevent water contact, and handle fragile components carefully.
Interact with customers to identify complaints and log visible symptoms like water leakage, no heating, steam issues, or burnt smell.
Conduct basic tests: power input, continuity, thermostat response, coil resistance, switch function, and tank heating.
Disassemble appliance safely to inspect internal components and diagnose faults such as blocked nozzles, leaky tanks, or faulty coils.
Replace or repair defective components like heating coil, fuse, cord, thermostat, tank, or steamer nozzle.
Reassemble parts ensuring safe connections, leak-free water components, and correct alignment of heating units.
Test appliance post-repair for proper heating, auto shut-off, continuous steam generation, and absence of leakage or blockage.
Demonstrate appliance operation to the customer, educate on usage and maintenance, complete documentation, collect payment if applicable, and maintain a clean work area.
